BiblicalUsage: Nachash is the serpent, and it runs from the garden to the end of the age. In Genesis 3:1 the serpent is more subtil than any beast of the field, and speaks to the woman, and in Numbers 21:9 Moses makes a serpent of brass and sets it on a pole, so that whoever looks on it shall live. In Psalm 58:4 the wicked have poison like the poison of a serpent, and in Isaiah 27:1 the Lord will punish leviathan the piercing serpent with His sore and great sword.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the serpent is the Bible's oldest enemy and its strangest picture of salvation at once. The same shape that brought death in the garden is lifted on a pole to give life in the wilderness, and the sword in Isaiah is the promise that the serpent does not win. I hold that the seed of the woman has crushed the serpent's head.
